Elson, Harley, Dodkin, Snell, Chandler, Dodkin, Boddington, Willis, Speechley, Holman, Rathbone, and others are training and from these men it should be possible to find eight to retain the "Nijmegen" Shield, and four to regain the National Championship.
Rickards, Bentley, Martin and Bidgood have been the high-lights, but Rathbone, Willis, Boddington, Jarvis, Allen and White have also played their part.

Speechley, Charlie Churcher, Storey, Redgrave, Reg Elson, Salter, Jones, Thorn, Dodkin, Brian, Boddington, Heather, Rutland, and all the others who may be called upon all know the value of a careful, studied, steady preparation and we may be sure of a team of determined, fit, walkers to do justice t…
Elson and Boddington still have something in hand, and our younger brigade had valuable experience which should be of great help to them in the future.
Lack of training consequent upon heavy business duties was telling its tale! BODDINGTON had the distinction of leading the “B” team home. Room will have to be found in the “A” team next year for him!
Stan Goold in his first race for us showed that he will be very useful. Boddington, Snell, Clark and Jarvis all put up creditable shows, as did also C.
Elson, Brian, Readman, Goold and Boddington (to mention a few) would have fared, had it been possible for them to turn out.

Elson, Heather, Goold, Jarvis, Boddington, Snell Hamer, Spooner, Cornish, Joe Coleman, Earle, Urry, Clark, Pattenden, Willis, True and several others, some beginners, who are showing rapid improvement.
Boddington, Clark, Earle, and Jarvis, being second. Fifteen of the first 52 to finish the course were Belgrave Harriers, which is a splendid indication of good all-round strength.

A "B" team, consisting of Boddington, Clark, Cornish, Martin, Snell, Reeve and Sutton also started. From the start our walkers were prominent, together with those of Surrey W.C. and Leicester W.C.—the three teams securing the placings in last year's race.
